evidence: Line 61 is the pass report of a two-branch check, not a check of its own: the Err branch at lines 56-59 records the same check name with false, and Checks::holds pushes a miss when false and finish() asserts no misses (f601_common/mod.rs:52-60). So the check 'solve succeeds' can fail. 'With the gap tolerance 1e-8' is enforced by the library, not by the test: ContactOptions::new(1, 1e-8) sets penetration_tolerance = 1e-8 and max_augmentations = 20 (src/contact.rs:194-198); the driver accepts a step only when no active node has |gap| above the tolerance (src/contact.rs:2404-2406, 2418) and otherwise returns Err 'the gap tolerance ... not met after ... augmentations' (src/contact.rs:2447-2456). Ok therefore implies the tolerance was met; the printed penetration (line 70; 9.7e-9 and 9.5e-9 in ADR 0571 lines 223-224) is the same quantity. The readers could not see contact.rs. The same idiom is used in sa_contact_mortar_hertz_f623.rs:48 and sa_contact_tl_fallback_f639.rs:308.
fix: None needed; optionally assert s.solves.last().penetration <= 1e-8 in the test so the clause is visible without reading the driver.

evidence: True as stated for the planned mutations: the section is doubly symmetric, the pre-stress is a pure axial force and the load a pure torque, so the bending block gets a zero right-hand side and no coupling entry; ADR 0585 itself registers the estimate as exactly 0 (line 223), states the decoupling (lines 93-94, 165) and records 0 (line 297). Omitting, negating or doubling K_sigma (Z1, Z2, Z5, lines 233-237) leaves the ratio at 0, and HB- is named as catcher for none of the seven mutations (lines 233-239) and appears in none of the 'caught by' rows (lines 308-314), so the record never shows it failing. Overstated by the readers: it is not a check that cannot fail. The warping geometric stiffness does contain twist-bending coupling terms driven by the end moments and shear forces of the pre-stress (src/beam_warping.rs:523-526, 715), which vanish here only because the from_static pre-stress has no moments; an error that put the axial force into a moment slot, or a wrong index of K_sigma into bending equations, would make HB- non-zero. So it guards a narrow class of error whose detection was never demonstrated, and it is not needed by the acceptance. Separate wording slip: ADR 0585 lines 226-227 list HB- under 'Negative controls', which it is not (it is a structural-zero check expected to pass).
fix: Add one mutation that HB- must catch (for example a non-zero end moment fed into the coupling term, or K_sigma indexed one component off), or state in the ADR that HB- is a structural-zero guard with no demonstrated failure; and take it out of the 'negative controls' sentence.

evidence: True as stated: the limit 0.15 on HS20m-M (line 225) and HS10m-M (226) is the ADR's own choice (these two are supporting checks, clause '(D5)', not in the acceptance) and stands against its own estimate of 2 to 6 percent (line 201, repeated in the row); measured 1.35e-2 and 3.40e-2 (lines 306-307), so the slack is 4 to 11 times. The readers' arithmetic is right: a uniform pressure on the Hertz disc gives M2/M0 = a^2/2, a_M = sqrt(5/4) a = 1.118 a, error 0.118, a pass; the test applies exactly this limit (sa_contact_tl_fallback_f639.rs:344-348). What limits the consequence: (1) on lines 222-223 (HS20f, HS10f) 0.15 is the acceptance's own radius limit (line 24, clause c3), not chosen by the ADR, and line 225 copies it; (2) the limit is not empty, the nodal-fit reading of the same four states gives 0.47, NaN, 0.21 and 4.89 (lines 316-317) and would miss it; (3) the uniform-pressure case is caught elsewhere: its peak is 2/3 of p_H, error 0.33 against the peak limit 0.20 on HS20f/HS10f (test line 350), and the peak of the linear solves was met at 2.5e-2 and below in ADR 0551 (ADR 0570 line 70); (4) the measured values are recorded, so the reader of the record sees 1.4e-2 and 3.4e-2, not 0.15. The moment radius is by construction an insensitive (integral) measure, which the ADR says at lines 165-167 but does not weigh against the limit.
fix: In a follow-up registration set the supporting limit near the estimate (about 0.08 for HS20m-M and HS10m-M), or add a sentence that the moment radius alone does not test the pressure shape and is to be read together with the peak check.

evidence: The figure is arithmetically right ((126.5 - 97.5) / 126.5 = 22.9 percent, from the H1 row at line 286) and it is a record, not a check: the acceptance (line 24) has no time clause and H1 registers the wall time as 'recorded' only (line 167), so the 'done' decision does not rest on it. The readers' point stands as stated, though: it is one run of each order, in a fixed sequence (levels first, then coordinates, line 167), on a machine the same paragraph calls shared, where the levels run took 126.5 s against ADR 0509's 77.7 s for the same computation (lines 293-295), a 63 percent load effect that is larger than the 23 percent difference reported. evidence: The slack is as the readers say (limit 1e-9 at lines 159-160 and crates/rcfd-linalg/tests/sa_eigen_points.rs:101 and :115, measured 6.325e-14 and 6.303e-14 at ADR lines 278-279), but the limit is not one that tests nothing. (1) It is the limit of the check it repeats, ADR 0509 L5 (docs/adr/0509-...md:221, same matrix, same closed form, `<= 1e-9`, measured 6.125e-14 at :323), and the acceptance's own figure for frequencies (ADR 0531 line 24, 1e-9). (2) It is at the tight end of the project's class for agreement with a closed form that is exact for the discrete problem: docs/process/tolerances.md:17 gives `<= 1e-6` to `<= 1e-9`. (3) The defects P1/P2 are there to catch (points applied with a wrong permutation, a factor or solve in the wrong order) give errors of order 1, not 1e-10; the kernel is the same supernodal factor in both orders, only the order differs. (4) The fine effect of the point order is checked elsewhere and separately: N3 requires the coordinate result to differ in bits from the level result (sa_eigen_points.rs:167-181, moved to the 10^3 grid by amendment 1, ADR lines 240-245), U1 checks the order used, E1 checks residuals `<= 1e-10` and H1 the 104 544-unknown cube. A loss of a few digits between 6e-14 and 1e-9 would pass P1/P2, which is true of every closed-form check in this class and is not specific to this item.
fix: None needed; if the project wants tighter closed-form limits it is a change to the tolerance table (docs/process/tolerances.md), not to this item.

evidence: The count of 9 is right as a count of factorisation calls, and the readers' contradiction is explained by the code: in crates/rcfd-fem/src/contact.rs:2220-2235 a convex iteration first calls factor_cached on the exact tangent, which is refused (SkylineError::Pivot), and then calls it again on the tangent without the curvature part; the record [(5, 2), (2, 0)] (ADR line 236) is therefore 7 + 2 = 9 calls. The two refused calls are not full factorisations: both factors return at the first refused pivot (crates/rcfd-linalg/src/sparse_chol.rs:558-563 for SparseLdlt, :1501-1512 for the supernodal one), and for the minimum-degree order the probe saw that refusal at position 4225 of 96 046 (ADR line 68), so the present driver's time is about 7 full factorisations plus two short ones: 7 x 186.45 = 1305 s against the measured 1456.59 s, which the ADR already puts down to load (line 243, 9 percent over A1-H). So 9 x 186 s was never claimed for t_p and the recorded times do not contradict the text. What is wrong is the wording and the arithmetic built on it: '82 s / 9 = 9.1 s per iteration' divides by 9 calls and calls the result per iteration (there are 7 iterations, 11.7 s each), and it treats the two refused supernodal attempts as full factorisations without any measurement of what a refused attempt costs in the nested-dissection order; the remaining gap to P1's 6.24 s is left unexplained. Nothing rests on it: T1 is 5.63e-2 against a limit of 1/3 (line 229).
fix: Reword line 245-246 to say the driver makes 9 factorisation calls (7 completed, 2 refused at the first non-positive pivot and of unmeasured cost), give the time per Newton iteration as 82 s / 7, and say that the excess over P1's 6.24 s per factor is not broken down.

evidence: The attribution holds for C1 and does not follow for the A checks. C1: FE 607505.8 below 609657.1 by 3.5e-3 (line 400), the sign and size of the registered shear term E I_z k^2/(kappa G A) = 3.5e-3 (line 195). A checks: the registration says shear flexibility lowers P_y and so M 'by about half of it at most' (lines 194-196), but A1' and A2' are above the closed form (178684.2 > 178454.6, 53979.8 > 53958.8, lines 390-391) and depend on the mesh (A4'' at 8 elements 2.1e-3 and 6.5e-4, line 396, against 1.29e-3 and 3.9e-4 at 16), so part of the error is discretisation and the sign is opposite to the shear prediction. The registration already knew this (line 196: 'ADR 0546 measured +5.9e-4 where it estimated -1e-3'), and ADR 0546:339-342 says of the same excess 'The difference is the element's lateral plane together with the coupling theta_z = psi of ADR 0508. So 'accounts for the size of the A ... errors' restates an undiagnosed cause as a finding; the comparison with the Euler-Bernoulli prototype (1e-6) shows only that the Timoshenko element differs, not that shear flexibility is the mechanism. 'About the same relative amount as in ADR 0546' is loose: 5.9e-4 there against 1.29e-3 (2.2 times) and 3.9e-4 (0.66 times) here. No check or limit depends on the sentence (limit 2e-2).
fix: Reword: C1 is below its closed form by the registered shear amount; the A values are above the closed form (opposite to the shear estimate, mesh-dependent, 0.7 to 2.2 times the ADR 0546 excess) and the cause is not diagnosed, as in ADR 0546.
